{{nihongo|'''Inaba Shrine'''|伊奈波神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mino Province]].

== Overview ==
[[File:Inaba-jinja Gifu Japan03-r.jpg|thumb|250px|Rōmon (two-storey gate)]]
[[File:Inaba-jinja Gifu Japan05-r.jpg|thumb|250px|Shinmon (shrine gate)]]
'''Inaba Shrine''' (伊奈波神社, いなばじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|lt=Shinto shrine|lt_ja=神社}} on Inaba-dōri, {{ill|Gifu, Gifu|ja|岐阜市|lt=Gifu|lt_ja=岐阜市}}, {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|ja|岐阜県|lt=Gifu Prefecture|lt_ja=岐阜県}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|ja|論社|lt=Shikinai ronsha|lt_ja=式内論社}} (a candidate for a small Shikinaisha) and the {{ill|Ichinomiya|ja|一宮|lt=sannomiya|lt_ja=三宮}} of {{ill|Mino Province|ja|美濃国|lt=Mino Province|lt_ja=美濃国}}. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ja|近代社格制度|lt=former shrine ranking system|lt_ja=旧社格}} it was a {{ill|Kokuhei Shōsha|ja|国幣小社|lt=Kokuhei Shōsha|lt_ja=国幣小社}}; it is now a {{ill|Beppyo shrine|ja|別表神社|lt=Beppyo shrine|lt_ja=別表神社}} and a {{ill|Kinpei-sha|ja|金幣社|lt=Kinpei-sha|lt_ja=金幣社}}. Tradition dates its founding to the fourteenth year of {{ill|Emperor Keikō|ja|景行天皇|lt=Emperor Keikō|lt_ja=景行天皇}}. Its annual festival is on 5 April ({{ill|Gifu Festival|ja|岐阜まつり|lt=Gifu Festival|lt_ja=岐阜まつり}}).

On 24 April 2015 (Heisei 27) it was recognised as {{ill|Japan Heritage|ja|日本遺産|lt=Japan Heritage|lt_ja=日本遺産}}, as a component of "Gifu, a Sengoku castle town where Lord Nobunaga's hospitality lives on".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story006/ |title="Nobunaga-kō no omotenashi" ga ikizuku Sengoku jōkamachi Gifu |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=2020-09-20 }}</ref>

=== Deities ===
The principal {{ill|Saijin|ja|祭神|lt=deity|lt_ja=祭神}} is {{ill|Prince Inishikiirihiko|ja|五十瓊敷入彦命|lt=Inishikiirihiko no Mikoto|lt_ja=五十瓊敷入彦命}} (いにしきいりひこのみこと), first son of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇|lt=Emperor Suinin|lt_ja=垂仁天皇}} and the god who opened up this land. Enshrined with him are his consort {{ill|Nunoshi-hime|ja|淳熨斗媛命|lt=Nunoshi-hime no Mikoto|lt_ja=淳熨斗媛命}} (ぬのしひめのみこと), his mother {{ill|Hibasu-hime|ja|日葉酢媛命|lt=Hibasu-hime no Mikoto|lt_ja=日葉酢媛命}} (ひばすひめのみこと), his maternal grandfather Hikotatsuhiko no Mikoto (ひこたつひこのみこと, ancestor of the {{ill|Inaba no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|稲葉国造|lt=Inaba no Kuni no Miyatsuko|lt_ja=稲葉国造}}), and his retainer {{ill|Mononobe no Tōchine|ja|物部十千根|lt=Mononobe no Tōchine no Mikoto|lt_ja=物部十千根命}} (もののべのとちねのみこと). Together they are called the Inaba Ōkami.

According to the shrine's tradition, Inishikiirihiko pacified Ōshū on the court's orders, but Toyomasu, governor of Mutsu, jealous of his success, slandered him; he was declared an enemy of the court and killed at the site of the present shrine.

== History ==
According to the shrine's tradition, it began in the fourteenth year of Emperor Keikō when {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|ja|武内宿禰|lt=Takenouchi no Sukune|lt_ja=武内宿禰}} enshrined Inishikiirihiko at Tsubakihara, north-west of {{ill|Mount Kinka (Gifu)|ja|金華山 (岐阜県)|lt=Mount Kinka|lt_ja=金華山}} (Maruyama, now inside {{ill|Gifu Park|ja|岐阜公園|lt=Gifu Park|lt_ja=岐阜公園}}). {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|天武天皇|lt=Emperor Tenmu|lt_ja=天武天皇}} is said to have prayed here for victory in the {{ill|Jinshin War|ja|壬申の乱|lt=Jinshin War|lt_ja=壬申の乱}}.

In {{ill|Tenbun|ja|天文 (元号)|lt=Tenbun|lt_ja=天文}} 8 (1539), when {{ill|Saitō Dōsan|ja|斎藤道三|lt=Saitō Dōsan|lt_ja=斎藤道三}} built Inabayama Castle ({{ill|Gifu Castle|ja|岐阜城|lt=Gifu Castle|lt_ja=岐阜城}}) on Mount Inaba, the shrine was moved to its present site. The Mononobe Shrine there, enshrining Mononobe no Tōchine, was merged into it, and it became the guardian shrine of Inabayama Castle. It was thereafter deeply revered as the general ''ubusunagami'' (tutelary deity) of Gifu. It was ranked a prefectural shrine in Meiji 6 (1873) and raised to {{ill|Kokuhei Shōsha|ja|国幣小社|lt=Kokuhei Shōsha|lt_ja=国幣小社}} in Shōwa 14 (1939). After the war, on 1 July 1952 (Shōwa 27), the Gifu Prefecture Jinjachō designated it a shrine visited by the head of the prefectural Jinjachō ({{ill|Kinpei-sha|ja|金幣社|lt=Kinpei-sha|lt_ja=金幣社}}, gold grade 3).{{sfn|Kimura|1997|p=9}}

The ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=延喜式神名帳}}'' does not list an "Inaba Shrine" among the shrines of Atsumi District, Mino Province, but it lists a small "Mononobe Shrine", which is held to be the Mononobe Shrine merged into this one. Another view holds that this shrine itself is the Shikinai Mononobe Shrine. The ''Mino no Kuni Jinmyōchō'' lists "Inaba Ōkami, Senior First Rank" and "Mononobe Myōjin, Junior Fifth Rank Lower".

== Facilities ==
All the buildings were lost to fire in the {{ill|1891 Mino–Owari earthquake|ja|濃尾地震|lt=Mino–Owari earthquake|lt_ja=濃尾地震}} of Meiji 24 (1891); the honden was rebuilt the following year. The present buildings were then built between Shōwa 4 (1929) and Shōwa 15 (1940) to the design of {{ill|Kōzō Nihonmatsu|ja|二本松孝蔵|lt=Nihonmatsu Kōzō|lt_ja=二本松孝蔵}}.<ref>Inaba Jinja Hōsankai, ''Inaba Jinja Ryakushi'' (Inaba Shrine, 1941).</ref>
* Torii (first and second torii), yōhaisho (place for worship from afar)
* Shinkyō (sacred bridge)
* Rōmon, shinmon
* Haiden, heiden, honden
* Shrine office, assembly hall, west hall
* Suigetsu-tei (tea room)

== Festivals ==
* 3 February: Setsubun festival. Special Setsubun prayers from 9:00 to 20:00, and from 18:00 a dedication of hand-held fireworks (''tezutsu hanabi''; about 110 of them) to drive away misfortune.
* 5 April:<ref>''Nenchū Gyōji Jiten'', p. 56, ed. {{ill|Masayoshi Nishitsunoi|ja|西角井正慶|lt=Nishitsunoi Masayoshi|lt_ja=西角井正慶}} (Tōkyōdō Shuppan, first ed. 23 May 1958).</ref> held jointly with {{ill|Kogane Shrine|ja|金神社|lt=Kogane Shrine|lt_ja=金神社}} (enshrining the consort Nunoshi-hime) and {{ill|Kashimori Shrine|ja|橿森神社|lt=Kashimori Shrine|lt_ja=橿森神社}} (enshrining their son Ichihayao no Mikoto) in the same city, and called the {{ill|Gifu Festival|ja|岐阜まつり|lt=Gifu Festival|lt_ja=岐阜まつり}}.

== Cultural properties ==
; Important Cultural Property (national)
* ''Tachi'' sword signed Kageyori-zō<ref name="bunkazaiichiran">{{Cite web|date=2012-04-06 |url=http://www.city.gifu.lg.jp/8875.htm |title=List of designated cultural properties in Gifu City |publisher=Gifu City |accessdate=2013-04-26}}</ref>

; Gifu Prefecture designated Important Cultural Properties
* Stone ''komainu''<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pref.gifu.lg.jp/kyoiku-bunka-sports/bunka-geijutsu/bunkazai-zuroku/bunkazai-zuroku/tyoukoku/gifusi/sekizoukomainu.html |title=Sekizō komainu |publisher=Gifu Prefecture |accessdate=2013-04-26}}</ref>
* Wooden lion head<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pref.gifu.lg.jp/kyoiku-bunka-sports/bunka-geijutsu/bunkazai-zuroku/bunkazai-zuroku/kougeihin/gifusi/shishigashira.html |title=Shishigashira |publisher=Gifu Prefecture |accessdate=2013-04-26}}</ref>
* ''Mino no Kuni Daisan-gū Inaba-sha Hon-engi'' (origin record of Inaba-sha, third shrine of Mino)<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pref.gifu.lg.jp/kyoiku-bunka-sports/bunka-geijutsu/bunkazai-zuroku/bunkazai-zuroku/syoseki/gifusi/minokoku.html |title=Mino no Kuni Daisan-gū Inaba-sha Hon-engi |publisher=Gifu Prefecture |accessdate=2013-04-26}}</ref>, 2 scrolls

=== Gifu City designated cultural properties ===
* Map of the ruins of Inaba Castle
; Gifu City designated tangible folk cultural property
* Four festival floats (''dashi'')<ref name="bunkazaiichiran"/>

=== Gifu City designated intangible folk cultural property ===
* The Gifu Festival rites accompanying the Inaba Shrine festival

== Goshuin ==
The shrine takes part in the "golden goshuin" project organised by the Gifu community group Hitohito no Kai, held as of November 2019 (Reiwa 1) at thirteen places in Gifu Prefecture.<ref name="kinnnogoshuin">The thirteen places: {{ill|Kogane Shrine|ja|金神社|lt=Kogane Shrine|lt_ja=金神社}}, Gyokushō-in, Gifu Nobunaga Shrine, Kōbu-ji, Osshin-ji, Inaba Shrine, {{ill|Gifu Castle|ja|岐阜城|lt=Gifu Castle|lt_ja=岐阜城}}, Tenryū-ji, Sōkyū-ji, Gokoku-ji, Shinchō-ji, Oniiwa Park and {{ill|Gujō Hachiman Castle|ja|郡上八幡城|lt=Gujō Hachiman Castle|lt_ja=郡上八幡城}}.</ref> On the last Friday of each month only, a goshuin decorated with gold, different from the usual one, is issued.<ref name="kinnnogoshuinaug">''Chūnichi Shimbun'', morning edition, Gifu edition, 29 August 2019, p. 16.</ref><ref name="kinnnogoshuinnov">''Chūnichi Shimbun'', morning edition, Gifu edition, 29 November 2019, p. 19.</ref>

== Access ==
; Public transport (bus)
: From JR {{ill|Gifu Station|ja|岐阜駅|lt=Gifu Station|lt_ja=岐阜駅}} or {{ill|Meitetsu Gifu Station|ja|名鉄岐阜駅|lt=Meitetsu Gifu Station|lt_ja=名鉄岐阜駅}}, take a {{ill|Gifu Bus|ja|岐阜乗合自動車|lt=Gifu Bus|lt_ja=岐阜バス}} "N80 Takatomi" or other N-route bus (N32–N86) towards Gifu Park / Nagara Bridge, or the "city loop, anticlockwise", about 10 minutes; get off at "Inaba-dōri" and walk about 7 minutes.

; Other
: About 20 minutes by bicycle from JR Gifu Station, where rental bicycles are available.
